STEP 1 - Scene: This is not really a meal; it is a single whole apple (red-yellow, likely a Gala-type) resting on a white triangular/angled plate. Photo is taken from a high-ish, oblique angle looking down at the plate.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is roughly triangular/rounded, about 26 cm across its longest undistorted width (side plate-sized, perhaps slightly larger). Area ≈ 530 cm² for a 26 cm round equivalent, though the actual plate shape is smaller; I use ~400 cm² effective. The apple is about 7–8 cm in diameter by visual comparison with the plate.

STEP 3 - Items: One whole apple (raw fruit).

STEP 4 - Area: Apple footprint ≈ 3.14 x (3.75)² ≈ 44 cm², about 11% of the ~400 cm² plate area.

STEP 5 - Volume: An apple is roughly a sphere-like ellipsoid, about 7.5 cm x 7 cm, so volume ≈ 4/3 x π x 3.75 x 3.75 x 3.5 ≈ 206 ml (gross envelope, whole fruit).

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole fruit is dense, roughly 0.85–0.9 g/ml for a whole apple (it is not a loose cut piece). 206 ml x 0.85 ≈ 175 g. A medium apple typically weighs about 150–180 g, consistent.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw apple ≈ 52 kcal per 100 g. 175 g x 0.52 ≈ 91 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single medium apple of ~175 g and ~90 kcal is plausible for what is visible. No other food is on the plate; the bowls at the bottom-right edge are not part of this item.

Estimate: about 175 g, about 90 kcal.
